text:
Pontus Holmberg is pointless in seven straight games, and this time the chances thinned out with the points: 3.1 expected points in that run, and only 1.8 individual expected goals over his last ten. His Nov. 8 two-goal game against Winnipeg is the last time he scored. He also played just 6.6 minutes against Carolina on Nov. 25.

The season as a whole is fine for a sixth-round pick in a 14.5-minute role. Six goals on 5.5 expected is fair finishing, and Tampa Bay gets 53.1% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on. His scoring rate earlier ran ahead of where we think his talent sits (2.24 points per 60 against a central estimate of 1.74), so the dry spell partly evens that out.

His real value sits elsewhere. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.23 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there last season, 99th percentile, plus 2.5 goals from drawing more penalties than he takes. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 9.4 primary shot assists per 60, 91st percentile. That's a useful player having a quiet month.
headline: Holmberg's points dried up, his value didn't
